sources.entry: A pastebin is a type of online content-hosting service used for sharing and storing code and text.

summary.name: Pastebin
summary.one_liner: Pastebin is a type of online text-hosting service for storing and sharing plain text such as source code snippets or error logs, with the best-known instance being pastebin.com (created 2002).
use_cases: sharing large text blocks in IRC chatrooms
self-hosting a private text sharing service
summary.what_it_does: The page describes pastebins as online content-hosting services where users store plain text entries called pastes. Registered users can create, edit, and delete their pastes, and can set them as public or private. Some pastebins add features such as commenting, rendering markup like Markdown or ReStructuredText, or version control. The page notes that several open source pastebin applications exist for self-hosting. It also gives history: pastebins were developed in the late 1990s to share large blocks of text in IRC chatrooms, and the pastebin.com site was later involved in a 2012 controversy over monitoring for leaked data.
notable: Pastebin.com, the most well-known pastebin, created in 2002
Several open source pastebin applications available for self-hosting
Optional markup rendering (Markdown, ReStructuredText), commenting, and version control on some platforms
caveats: The page is a general Wikipedia overview of the category and does not describe a single product's pricing or limits
Page notes it needs more citations and some lead content is not repeated elsewhere in the article
